opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Head office, marketing support and running the global franchising machine — $701M of SG&A (including $106M of depreciation and amortization), plus $29M of other operating expense, net.

footerNote: The release's printed lines are rounded: interest expense less nonoperating income sums to $372M, while printed pre-tax income of $2,861M implies $371M of net other expense; this page follows the printed pre-tax total and net income.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+4% in constant currencies)

oneTimers: Pre-tax charges of $43M ($0.05 per share), primarily restructuring charges under the 'Accelerating the Organization' program to modernize how the company works; excluding them, operating income rose 7% and EPS was $3.19.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $390M on McDonald's debt, partly offset by $18M of net nonoperating income.
segmentNote: Systemwide sales grew 8% (6% in constant currency); comparable sales: U.S. +2.5%, International Operated Markets +4.0%, International Developmental Licensed Markets +5.6%.

segments.name: Franchised restaurants
segments.note: Rent and royalties paid by the local owners who run most McDonald's restaurants — the heart of the business model.

segments.name: Company-owned restaurants
segments.note: Food and drink sold at restaurants McDonald's runs itself.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Fees from franchisees for technology and digital platforms, plus brand-licensing income — nearly double a year ago.

takeaways.text: Global comparable sales rose 3.8% — the U.S. +2.5%, International Operated Markets +4.0% and licensed markets +5.6%, led by Japan. Systemwide sales rose 8%.
takeaways.title: Comps rose across the board

takeaways.text: Diluted EPS was $3.14, up 12%. Excluding $43M of pre-tax restructuring charges under 'Accelerating the Organization', it was $3.19. Net income was $2,253M.
takeaways.title: EPS rose 12%

takeaways.text: Franchise revenue — rent and royalties from other people's restaurants — was $4.2B, 62% of all revenue, and grew 7%. Company-run store sales were flat at $2.5B at much thinner margins.
takeaways.title: Franchisees carry the model

verdict: McDonald's grew revenue 5% to $6.8B and operating income 11% to $3.2B — comparable sales rose 3.8% across every segment — as franchise rent and royalties grew 7% while company-run restaurant sales stayed flat.
